title: AI trading tool for eToro user portfolio
author: BenefitGrand8752
selftext:
eToro recently launched “private” portfolios that users can manage through their own AI applications. I tried building an app for automated portfolio management, cloning the look and feel of the eToro app, but I’m sure they’ll forgive me...

Aside from a few technical choices by eToro that I don’t entirely agree with, I’ve been trying it out for the past few days. I’ve also put together a short introductory video. The app language is italian by now (but provide a multilingual version is possible, llm language prompt translation aside...).

For now, the app is experimental, and I’m still testing it. If it holds up on all fronts, I’ll consider whether it makes sense to put it on GitHub.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
eToro opening private portfolios to outside apps changes what your clone has to worry about: rebalancing what's already held and opening something new are very different permissions, and an LLM in the loop makes that line matter. getting that line right took me longer than anything else when I built Quantradin. agents trade a paper equities book there, free, and opening anything takes a key you hand over yourself. quantradin.com

does your app open new positions on its own or only resize existing ones?

replies.author: BenefitGrand8752
replies.body:
Yes, it opens/closes positions on its own, but only ones a rule already names. The LLM only helps me write the rules: plain language becomes fixed rules that I review before switching them on. It’s never in the trading loop, so nothing it produces at runtime can place an order. Each rule states the asset, the size (% of available cash), the stop loss and how long it stays active.

The hard line is the keys. The app trades only a separate agent portfolio with its own keys. The main account’s keys are read-only, and the app refuses keys that have trading scope. My real money sits in a copy of that portfolio with a copy stop loss. There’s also a manual mode where every order waits for my approval.

The app have also llm fired rules, but frankly by now it did not performed as I would like to. AI helps me to select assets with certain profiles (risk, performance ecc...) but it is an offline process

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: LLM writes the rule once, you review it, then it's frozen. that's the version I'd trust too. the spot I'd stress-test is sizing off available cash: after a run of wins or losses the same 5% rule is a very different bet than on day one, and nobody reviews that drift.

comments.author: investigatormaker
comments.body:
Since eToro's private portfolios are driven by your own AI app, the first thing people will ask before trusting it is what the model does on its own: place orders, rebalance, or only suggest. Before it goes to GitHub, a README stating that, plus whatever limits you set (maximum position size, a daily trade cap, a manual approval step), would matter more than the multilingual version. I'd also give it its own look instead of the cloned eToro interface, so nobody mistakes it for an official app. How long have you let it run on the portfolio unattended?

replies.author: BenefitGrand8752
replies.body:
Good points. Here’s what the README will say.

**What it does:** all three. It buys and sells on its own, it rebalances (rotation rules close one position and move the proceeds into another), and it can just suggest: in manual mode every order is a proposal you approve.

**How you build a strategy:** describe it in natural language, or start from the built-in library. The LLM compiles your text into a deterministic rule, and you review it before it goes live. The model is never in the trading loop: a deterministic engine runs the rules. A rule can be as specific as this:

>*On closed 1-minute RKLB candles, if the close crosses above the lower Bollinger band (30 periods, 3 standard deviations) and the close is above the 400-period SMA, buy RKLB with 20% of available cash, stop loss at 3% of the invested amount.*

A strategy can hold up to 100 rules: entries, exits, rotations between assets, calendar rules (e.g. “the 4th-last trading day of the month”), holding-time exits and native stop loss / take profit.

**Testing:** besides classic backtests, every strategy can run in **shadow mode**. It tracks the rule’s performance on live data over time without trading, then gives a verdict before you put money on it.

**Limits:**

* Each rule sets its size as a % of cash, plus its stop loss and lifetime.
* Per-strategy caps on max drawdown, daily loss and buys per day block new entries.
* It trades only eToro Agent Portfolios, as many as you like, each with its own keys. It never trades the main account: those keys are read-only, and keys with trading scope are refused there.
* I copy my agent portfolio with a whole copy stop loss.

**The look:** it already ships three templates. The eToro-style one is just one of them.

**Unattended:** it has been trading real money live since a week ago. Every decision is logged and pushed to Telegram. Redoundance, restart and alive monitoring are also provided

The plan is to release it as open source. It is a proof of concept for me.
